compliance.title: For Schools: Safety & Compliance
compliance.kidIntro: Hi teachers and grown-ups! SpArki is built to be safe, simple, and respectful of kids’ privacy.
compliance.quickFact2: Kid progress can stay on-device, and school progress can be anonymous.
compliance.quickFact3: Teachers can use class codes instead of student names.
compliance.quickFact4: We aim to follow COPPA, FERPA, and CIPA best practices.
compliance.coppaBody: We design SpArki to avoid collecting children’s personal information. For school pilots, we recommend using anonymous student codes (for example: Explorer-42) rather than names or emails.
compliance.ferpaBody: For school use, we treat progress data as an education record. We recommend schools avoid entering student names. Teachers can export class progress as CSV for their own records.
compliance.cipaBody: SpArki teaches safe and kind online behavior and supports school-safe use. Schools should still apply their own filtering and device policies.
compliance.dataPrivacy2: No third-party analytics in the kid experience.
compliance.dataPrivacy3: Progress can be stored locally or synced anonymously for schools.

governance.pageIntro: Use this page to brief superintendents, county offices, and boards on how SpArki handles student data and AI. It complements the full compliance checklist below.
governance.pageIntroShort: SpArki is built as a supplement to your existing curriculum and systems—not a replacement. AI assists with optional generation after teacher upload; educators remain in charge.
governance.packetFooter: This summary is informational. Schools should align use with local policy and legal counsel.
governance.dataFlowStep1: Teachers sign in with a school email. Class list and join codes live in your Supabase project under your control.
governance.dataFlowStep2: Students join with a class code and an anonymous label (e.g. Explorer-42). We recommend not using full student names in the product.
governance.dataFlowStep3: Progress syncs as JSON tied to that anonymous label—internet safety, AI & coding tracks, optional generated weekly units, and subject practice signals.
governance.dataFlowStep4: Optional: teachers upload a PDF for the weekly generator. Text is sent to OpenAI to draft units; source PDFs can be stored in private Supabase Storage for the pilot.
governance.dataFlowBody: Teacher account → SpArki (Supabase) → anonymous student progress rows; optional PDF → OpenAI → generated units stored in Supabase; no ads or behavioral profiling in the kid experience.
governance.aiUseWeekly: Weekly lesson generator: teacher-uploaded PDF text is summarized into three short units with practice and an optional Sparki-themed adventure layer—teachers review before assigning.
governance.aiUseHomework: Homework adventure (when enabled): image or text of a homework page may be analyzed to produce a guided, age-safe story prompt—grown-up consent and configuration apply.
governance.aiUseNoTraining: We do not use student chat or child content to train public AI models. Use commercial APIs per their terms; prefer minimal retention settings where available.
governance.studentIdTitle: Student identifiers — do this / avoid this
governance.studentIdDo: Do: use class codes plus anonymous labels; export CSV for your own gradebook mapping offline if the district requires it.
governance.studentIdDont: Avoid: pasting full rosters, student emails, or state IDs into bulletin or free-text fields.
governance.boardSummaryBody: SpArki delivers bilingual, standards-aligned digital citizenship and AI literacy for ages 3–11. Schools keep data in their own Supabase project; students can participate without full names; AI features are teacher-initiated supplements with clear human oversight.
governance.strategicLead: Artificial intelligence is becoming essential in education—and it carries real risks. We hold both: readiness means age-appropriate AI literacy for work and citizenship, while misuse can harm privacy, academic integrity, and trust. Public systems are integrating AI across levels; responsible adoption needs infrastructure that pairs security and ethics with classroom value.
governance.strategicPillar1: Safety barrier: reviews, access patterns, and policies that reduce fraud, academic misconduct, and privacy leaks—consistent with minimal student data and teacher-in-the-loop design.
governance.strategicPillar2: Workforce readiness: structured digital citizenship, AI literacy, and standards-aligned practice so learners build durable skills, not one-off shortcuts.
governance.strategicPillar3: Human-centered outcomes: age-safe tone, adult oversight, and respect for students’ wellbeing and intellectual growth—intelligence used in service of learners.
governance.strategicPillar4: Human–machine co-creation: AI can assist lesson preparation and multimodal resources when educators choose; generated material is reviewed before it reaches students where SpArki is configured that way.
governance.strategicPillar5: Algorithmic accountability: evaluation habits, content standards, and clear escalation when outputs are biased, incorrect, or inappropriate—keeping instructional judgment in charge.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.coppaBody: SpArki's Adventures Academy is designed for families and is committed to complying with the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 without verifiable parental consent.
privacy.noCollectTitle: Information We Do Not Collect from Children
privacy.noCollectBody: In the child-facing experience, we do not collect names, email addresses, photos, voice recordings, or any personally identifiable information (PII) from children. Children access content through a parent-managed session (e.g., a temporary link or this device after a parent has signed in). There is no child account or child login.
privacy.parentOnlyBody: Grown-ups sign in to access the Parent view, unlock the Safety Pass, and (when available) upload homework. Parent consent is required before any upload or processing of content that could contain a child's information. We recommend verifiable consent methods (e.g., as described in our parent materials) where applicable.
privacy.dataMinBody: When homework or similar content is processed, we use it only to generate a learning adventure. We do not store uploaded images or documents after processing. Only anonymized results (e.g., "math addition problem") may be kept in a session. We do not use child data for behavioral advertising or profiling.
privacy.progressBody: Progress (e.g., quiz scores, sparkles) may be stored locally on the device for the child's experience. We do not use cookies or tracking for child-directed sessions in a way that would support behavioral targeting.
privacy.schoolPilotsBody: When a school runs a pilot, teachers may sign in with an account; students may join with a class code using a minimal identifier (e.g., anonymous session or first-name code, depending on setup). Progress for school pilots may be stored with our database provider so teachers can view aggregated results. Optional features (e.g., homework image upload, read-aloud, or generated video) may send content or text to AI or voice providers only as described in your pilot agreement and this policy. Schools may request a subprocessor list and pilot terms before starting.
privacy.ageBandBody: For families, the app stores your selected age band (Sparki Tots, Kids, or Crew) in the browser to tailor lessons and saved progress per band. For schools, teachers may set an age band per class so generated weekly content matches that group. This is not used for advertising.
privacy.rightsBody: Parents can review, request deletion of, or revoke access to any data associated with their use of the service. For questions about this policy or to exercise your rights, please use our Contact page.

marketingPages.post1Title: Why we lead with internet safety
marketingPages.post1Excerpt: Screens are part of childhood — Sparki meets kids with stories, not fear.
marketingPages.post1Body:
Sparki Academy exists because families asked for something kinder than scare tactics.

We start with internet safety because trust has to come first. When children feel respected, they listen — and when parents see clear guardrails, they relax enough to learn together.

From there we grow into AI literacy, subject practice, and Tutor Academy — always with grown-ups in the loop.
marketingPages.post2Excerpt: Full subject depth, Homework Adventure, and Tutor Academy — one subscription.
marketingPages.post2Body:
Adventure Academy is our subscription tier for families who want the full Sparki stack.

You get structured practice across math, reading, science, and history, Homework Adventure uploads with SpArki-guided stories, and Tutor Academy for Socratic help matched to your state and age band.

We keep pricing family-sized because tutoring should not be a luxury good.
marketingPages.post3Excerpt: Turn a worksheet photo into a quest — with parent upload and consent.
marketingPages.post3Body:
Homework Adventure is built for real evenings: tired kids, busy adults, and math that suddenly looks different than when we were in school.

A grown-up uploads a clear photo, we analyze it safely, and SpArki turns the struggle into a short narrative quest. It is not magic — it is structure, encouragement, and a little delight when brains are fried.

Always review outputs together; you are still the teacher of record at home.

fairCodeBuilder.ch1_desc: You are building a system to recommend students for scholarships. Which rules should the code use?
fairCodeBuilder.ch1_lesson: Fair systems use ability and need (GPA, essays, need). Name, looks, and gender are not fair signals here.
fairCodeBuilder.ch2_desc: Picking players for a school team. What should your code look at?
fairCodeBuilder.ch2_lesson: Teams should reflect skill and fitness — not money, accent, or friend groups.
fairCodeBuilder.ch3_desc: Ranking candidates for a cashier job. Which rules matter?
fairCodeBuilder.ch3_lesson: Hiring should focus on skills and experience — not age, neighborhood, or school name alone.
fairCodeBuilder.ch4_desc: Your app recommends games. What data should it use?
fairCodeBuilder.ch4_lesson: Use real play behavior — not gender, country, or letters in a name.
fairCodeBuilder.ch5_desc: Recommending books to visitors. What should the system know?
fairCodeBuilder.ch5_lesson: Use reading habits and genres — not money, family background, or clothing.
